split: Latest 20% per user by rating timestamp; ties broken by movie ID. Item eligibility and popularity computed only from training data. Positive = rating >=4. At least 3 training positives and 1 eligible test positive.
evaluation: All eligible unseen items; no sampled negatives. Evaluate sparse positive top-80 model with the complete training-positive profile. This does not evaluate new users with 1–5 picks, group fairness, genre filters or shuffle.
limitations: Historical catalog through 2018, skewed toward English-language films and MovieLens participants.
Per-user temporal split is not a single global time cutoff; cross-user information can come from later timestamps.
Offline ratings metrics do not establish real-world satisfaction or reduced decision time.
This is a development snapshot experiment, not a standardized benchmark or state-of-the-art claim.

five_like_evaluation.protocol: Use last five eligible training likes per user, production 0.9 normalized affinity + 0.1 quality ranking; exclude all training-seen movies. Same held-out latest-20% split. Does not represent real new-user satisfaction.
